name: Australian First Nations fashion (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander)
description: Fashion labels of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander designers and art centres: artist prints on resort wear, swimwear and gowns, shown at the National Indigenous Fashion Awards.

name: Pasifika and Pacific Island fashion
description: Contemporary Polynesian, Melanesian and diaspora island wear: masi, tapa and bilum motifs on puletasi, robe mission (Mother Hubbard) dresses, shirts and resort sets.

name: Central Asian ethno-modern fashion
description: Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Uzbek couture and ready-to-wear that recuts nomadic and national dress (chapan, kamzol, felt, ornament) in modern shapes; shown at Almaty and Tashkent fashion weeks.

name: Central Asian ikat and suzani fashion (atlas, adras, chakan)
description: Couture and ready-to-wear in Margilan and Dushanbe atlas and adras ikat silks, suzani and chakan embroidery, often cut as chapans and quilted robes.

name: Armenian heritage and taraz revival fashion
description: Yerevan labels that research and rework Armenian costume, taraz ornament, manuscripts and alphabet into modern and festive clothing, backed by Yerevan Fashion Week.

name: Sri Lankan batik and handloom fashion
description: Contemporary Sri Lankan labels built on batik, beeralu lace, handloom and the Kandyan osariya, shown at Colombo Fashion Week.

name: Newar and Dhaka dress revival (Nepal)
description: Nepali revival and fusion of Newar dress and woven textiles (Haku Patasi, Dhaka, Chaubandi Cholo) cut as tailored coats, gowns and waistcoats.

name: Pakistani lawn and pret
description: Seasonal printed and embroidered lawn and khaddar suits sold unstitched or ready to wear by Pakistani houses such as Gul Ahmed, Khaadi, Sapphire and Alkaram.

name: Gaucho dress (bombachas de campo)
description: Argentine and Rioplatense horseman dress: bombachas de campo, alpargatas, berets, rastra belts and ponchos, sold by country-wear shops and makers such as Pampero.

name: Antillean madras dress (Wob Dwiyet, robe créole)
description: Creole women's dress of Dominica, Saint Lucia, Martinique and Guadeloupe: white chemise, lace petticoat, madras skirt and head tie, made by local couture labels.

name: Cholita and pollera dress (Andes)
description: Aymara and Quechua women's pollera dress of La Paz and Cusco (gathered skirts, fringed shawls, bowler hats), taken into high fashion by Bolivian and Peruvian designers.

name: Mexican artisan-textile fashion
description: Contemporary Mexican labels made with Indigenous weavers, embroiderers and leatherworkers, such as Carla Fernandez, Amor & Rosas and Colectiva Concepcion.

name: Indigenous North American fashion (First Nations, Inuit, Metis, Native American)
description: Indigenous designers of North America blending beadwork, ribbon work, regalia and nation-specific art with contemporary clothing; shown at Indigenous Fashion Weeks in Vancouver, Toronto and Santa Fe.

name: Baju Melayu and baju kurung (Malay national dress)
description: Malay baju Melayu for men and baju kurung for women, national dress of Malaysia and Brunei, sold for Raya and formal wear by local labels.

name: Sinh and pha sin (Lao and Thai tube skirt revival)
description: Handwoven tube skirt of Laos and northern and north-eastern Thailand, worn daily in Laos and recut by Thai and Lao labels into contemporary skirts and separates.

name: Southeast Asian handwoven textile fashion (songket, tenun, ikat, tais)
description: Contemporary clothing cut from hand-woven songket brocade, tenun, ikat and Timorese tais of Brunei, Malaysia, Indonesia and Timor-Leste.

name: Batik fashion
description: Clothing made from wax-resist dyed batik cloth, from Indonesian houses to Malaysian and Singaporean labels.

name: Modern Filipiniana (baro't saya and terno)
description: Philippine national women's dress of baro't saya and terno, reworked by contemporary designers in pina, jusi and local weaves.

name: Burmese longyi, htamein and inngyi
description: Myanmar national dress of longyi and htamein wrapped skirts with the inngyi top, modernised by Yangon boutiques.

name: Khmer sampot and krama
description: Cambodian wrapped sampot and krama cloth in silk and cotton, reworked by contemporary Cambodian labels.

name: Habesha kemis (Ethiopian and Eritrean highland dress)
description: Ethiopian and Eritrean long handwoven cotton dress with tilet embroidery, worn with the netela shawl; regional styles made by Addis Ababa designers.

name: Herero dress (ohorokova)
description: Namibian Herero women's long Victorian-style dress with layered petticoats and the horned otjikaiva headdress, sewn by designers for weddings and festivals.

name: Pantsula style
description: South African township dance subculture dressed in coordinated crews: Dickies work pants, bright collared shirts, Converse All Stars and small-brim caps.

name: Izikhothane (skhothane)
description: South African township culture of competitive display in loud designer labels (Carvela, Italian shirts, Versace), layered and discarded to show wealth; from Katlehong in the 2000s.

name: Seshoeshoe (shweshwe) dress
description: Dresses, skirts and wraps in discharge-printed shweshwe cotton, worn by married Sotho and Xhosa women and in contemporary South African fashion.

name: Post-Soviet streetwear and underground fashion
description: Russian and Georgian designer wear quoting 1990s gopnik dress and club culture: Cyrillic tees, tracksuits, cropped jeans; Gosha Rubchinskiy, Vetements and Tbilisi labels.

name: Slavic chic (folk-craft revival fashion)
description: Polish and Ukrainian designers reviving rural embroidery, lace, crochet, knitting and weaving in luxury and slow fashion; the term is credited to Magda Butrym.

name: Paninaro (paninari)
description: 1980s Milanese youth subculture built on expensive labels: Moncler puffers, Stone Island, C.P. Company, Best Company, Levi's 501s and Timberland boots.

name: Nautical and marinière style (Breton stripe, sailor dress)
description: French navy-derived Breton striped shirt and seafaring dress (pea coats, duffle coats, oilskins, sailor knits) worn as civilian fashion; Saint James, Armor Lux, Orcival.

name: Folk and heritage knitwear (Aran, gansey, lopapeysa, Cowichan, alpaca)
description: Regional knitwear: Irish Aran, Channel Island guernseys, Icelandic lopapeysur, Nordic patterned sweaters, Coast Salish Cowichan sweaters and Andean alpaca knits.

name: La Sape (sapeurs)
description: Dandy culture of Kinshasa and Brazzaville (Societe des Ambianceurs et des Personnes Elegantes): designer suits, silk socks, bright colours; Johannesburg swenkas compete similarly.

name: Faso Dan Fani fashion
description: Clothing in Burkina Faso's hand-woven Faso Dan Fani cotton strip cloth, from tees and polos to suits and dresses, promoted at Dan'Fani Fashion Week.

name: Bogolan fashion (Mali)
description: Couture and ready-to-wear built on Malian hand-dyed bogolan mud cloth by labels such as Haby Diallo, Gope Design and Farafina Tigne.

name: Kaba and slit (Ghana)
description: Ghanaian women's ensemble of fitted kaba blouse and long slit skirt, made up by couture houses such as Christie Brown and Pistis.

name: Adire and aso-oke fashion (Yoruba)
description: Nigerian labels working Yoruba adire resist-dyed cloth and hand-woven aso-oke, from Maki Oh and Shop Ayora to Kenneth Ize and Deola Sagoe.

name: Dolly kei
description: Vintage-style Japanese clothing drawing on European fairy tales and old-world folk dress, sometimes with religious symbols; associated with the Grimoire shop.

name: Kogal
description: Gyaru substyle on a high-school uniform base: shortened skirt, loose socks, scarf and often dyed hair.

name: Contemporary gho and kira fashion (Bhutan)
description: Bhutanese designers reworking the national gho and kira and handloom textiles into modern collections, shown at Bhutan Fashion Week 2025.

name: Sudanese toub fashion (teyab designers)
description: Designer labels, many online, selling the Sudanese toub wrap for day, evening and wedding wear in silk, chiffon and cotton, painted or beaded.

name: Palestinian heritage fashion (tatreez, Majdalawi, keffiyeh)
description: Contemporary Palestinian labels built on tatreez cross-stitch, Majdalawi weaving and the keffiyeh, from gowns and puffer coats to hoodies and abayas.

name: Algerian traditional couture (karakou, chedda, Kabyle dress, robe Naili)
description: Algerian couture houses specialising in the karakou, chedda, Kabyle dress, robe Naili and blouza wahrania, shown as haute couture.

name: Iranian manteau and rusari
description: Iranian women's everyday dress built on the manteau overcoat and rusari headscarf, with dozens of domestic brands dedicated to it.

name: Kurdish dress (şal û şapik, şemlek)
description: Kurdish men's shal u shapik ensemble and women's shemlek robe, qurte vest and coin headdress, reworked by ateliers in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah.

name: Techwear
description: High-performance, weather-ready urban clothing in dark palettes with technical fabrics and modular construction; Acronym and Veilance are cited names.

name: Old money (quiet luxury)
description: Understated, high-quality classic clothes signalling inherited wealth, also called stealth wealth or quiet luxury; the French BCBG is its Parisian form.

name: Japanese Ivy (Ametora)
description: Japanese movement perfecting American Ivy and preppy clothing with academic detail, begun in the 1960s with VAN Jacket.

name: Dark academia
description: Tweed jackets, pleated skirts, dark earthy palette and library imagery, tied to classics and literature.

name: Cottagecore
description: Pastoral nostalgia in soft natural-fibre clothing: prairie dresses, aprons and hand-knits, echoing Gunne Sax and Laura Ashley.

name: Preppy
description: Durable sportswear-based Northeastern campus style: polos, oxford shirts, chinos, cable knits, boat shoes; Spanish pijo and German poppers are national forms.

name: Normcore
description: Deliberately unremarkable everyday clothing: straight jeans, plain tees, chunky trainers, valuing fit and material over branding.

name: Neo-Chinese style
description: Everyday wear that simplifies traditional Chinese elements such as Mandarin collars and frog closures; popular on Xiaohongshu.

name: Guochao
description: National-trend movement favouring homegrown Chinese brands, from Li-Ning and Anta sportswear to streetwear labels using reinterpreted heritage motifs.

name: Mori kei (mori girl)
description: Japanese forest-dweller style of layered thin fabrics, earth tones and natural materials.

name: Fairy kei
description: Pastel, floaty Harajuku style from 1980s children's pop culture; tied to the Spank! shop (Tavuchi) and the magazines Zipper and Cutie.

name: Oshare kei
description: Bright, pop-flavoured visual kei branch with colourful costumes, decora touches, arm warmers and striped socks.

name: Girly kei (Larme kei)
description: Dainty feminine style from the magazine LARME for women in their 20s; Larme kei is the overseas label.

name: Y2K
description: Fashion of about 1997-2004 and its revival: low-rise flared jeans, baby tees, velour tracksuits, baggy jeans and jerseys; Japanese Heisei retro and Chinese qianxi feng included.

name: Minimalism
description: Quiet, simple clothing in white, neutral and muted tones, from designers such as Jil Sander, The Row and Lemaire.

name: Skate (skater)
description: Skateboarders' durable baggy clothing: graphic tees, loose jeans or cargo shorts and padded skate shoes from Vans, DC and Etnies.

name: Surf (surfer)
description: Beach and wave-riding dress: boardshorts, rash vests, wetsuits, logo tees and hoodies, from the Australian big three Quiksilver, Billabong and Rip Curl.

name: Jirai kei
description: Dark-girly Japanese style from about 2020: ribbons, lace, frilly skirts, black and pink palette, platform shoes; the softer ryosan-gata is a variant.

name: Ganguro
description: Mid-1990s Shibuya gyaru branch with deep tan, bleached hair, platform boots, miniskirts and hibiscus accessories.

name: Hime gyaru
description: Princess-gal branch of the late 2000s: frilly pastel dresses, layered skirts, lace, big curls, bows and tiaras.

name: Hime Lolita
description: Over-the-top princess lolita substyle, close to classic but borrowing sweet decoration.

name: Angura kei
description: Underground-theatre style of modified school uniforms, kimono and haori, Showa-era nostalgia and dark, theatrical makeup.

name: Biker
description: Motorcycle-culture dress of leather, black and red, studs, chains and denim, projecting toughness.

name: Rude boy
description: Jamaican ska-era street style of sharp suits, thin ties and pork pie or trilby hats; fed UK mod and skinhead dress.

name: Rockabilly
description: Exaggerated 1950s Americana dress: white tees, cuffed jeans and leather jackets; swing dresses and pin-up hair; cherry, dice and swallow motifs.

name: Gothabilly
description: Rockabilly crossed with goth: black silks, satin, lace, velvet, corsets, top hats, pinstripes and cat-eye glasses.

name: Psychobilly
description: Punkier rockabilly offshoot with tall quiffs, painted leather jackets and vests, band tees, brothel creepers or Dr. Martens, and horror and B-movie motifs.

name: Acubi
description: Korean minimalist Y2K evolution with subversive basics: bolero cardigans, cargo pants, baby tees, slim top over big pants.

name: Avant basic
description: Pastel, retro-psychedelic maximalism in geometric and animal prints; Lisa Says Gah, Paloma Wool and Ganni are associated.

name: Berlin techno fashion
description: Anonymous, utilitarian club dress with fetishwear elements, associated with Lueder, Ottolinger and Rick Owens.

name: Cult Party kei
description: Mostly secondhand Japanese style of sheer white and cream layers and religious imagery, named for the Cult Party shop.

name: Bodikon (bodycon)
description: Japan's 1985-94 body-conscious disco-era style worn in luxury and DC-brand pieces such as Pinky & Dianne.

name: Balletcore
description: 2020s ballet-inspired trend: tutus, wraps, leg warmers, tulle, satin, bows and ballet flats.

name: Goth punk (Japan)
description: Japanese visual-kei-adjacent mix of goth and punk: bondage trousers, studs, safety pins, buckled platform boots, silver chains.

name: Hippie
description: 1960s flower-power dress: tie-dye, bell-bottoms, peasant blouses, fringe, paisley, handmade beaded jewellery and sandals.

name: Nu-goth
description: 2010s sleek monochrome goth with occult symbols: black maxi skirts, oversized sweaters, harnesses, platform boots, silver jewellery.

name: Jojifuku
description: Adults wearing Japanese children's-brand clothing from 1989-2000s, such as Mezzo Piano and Pom Ponette, with mascot prints.

name: Kinderwhore
description: Early-1990s female punk and grunge look pairing babydoll and Peter Pan collar dresses with ripped tights and smudged makeup.

name: Marshmallow girl
description: Japanese yurufuwa (loose, fluffy) style of soft textures and rounded relaxed silhouettes for women outside the thin ideal.

name: Regencycore
description: 2020s Bridgerton-driven feminine style with puffed cap sleeves, empire waists, low necklines and corsets.

name: Peacock Revolution
description: Mid-1960s menswear movement of bright patterns, paisley, brocade suits, cravats, Nehru jackets, flares and winkle-picker boots.

name: Romantic goth
description: 1990s goth branch of flowing velvet gowns, lace dresses and ruffle-cuff poet shirts with corsetry.

name: Tecktonik
description: French electro-dance youth look of 2006-08: slim jeans, logo tees, fingerless gloves, LED belts, neon and punk crests.

name: Tenniscore
description: Tennis-whites microtrend: pleated skirts, polos, visors, cable knits and sweater vests from Lacoste, Wilson and Sporty & Rich.

name: VSCO girl
description: 2019 teen look of oversized tees, scrunchies, puka shells, Birkenstocks, Crocs or Vans, Fjallraven and Brandy Melville.

name: Black Ivy
description: Preppy dress by Black wearers blending navy blazers, tweed sets and varsity jackets with Ralph Lauren, Hilfiger, sneakers and chains.

name: Cholo (Chicano)
description: Chicano California style descended from pachuco dress, with later baggy work-style clothing.

name: Cholombiano
description: Monterrey cumbia dancers' oversized look: tumbadilla baggy clothes, Dickies, giant plaid or Hawaiian shirts, sculpted hair.

name: Deathrock
description: Punk-meets-goth: teased deathhawk, ripped fishnets, spiderweb sleeves, leather, lace, band tees and pale dramatic makeup.

name: Disco
description: 1970s nightclub glamour: polyester, clingy jersey, halter tops, jumpsuits, bell-bottoms and platform shoes.

name: E-girl and e-boy
description: Late-2010s TikTok blend of emo, scene, pop-punk and skater styles.

name: Eshay
description: Australian street style of branded sportswear: Nike TN Air Max Plus, puffer vests, Tommy Hilfiger, Ralph Lauren, chest bumbags.

name: Flaite
description: Chilean youth identity built on prestige brands such as Nike Jordans and Dunks, Adidas, Lacoste and Oakley.

name: Gabber
description: Dutch hardcore-techno fans in tracksuits, bomber jackets, Nike Air Max sneakers and shaved heads.

name: Garconne
description: 1920s French androgynous New Woman look: boyish linear silhouette, short hair, menswear borrowings.

name: Genderless kei
description: Harajuku mid-2010s style blurring masculine and feminine clothing, hair and makeup into a gender-neutral look.

name: Gopnik
description: Post-Soviet and Eastern-bloc working-class youth dress centred on Adidas, Puma and Nike tracksuits; the Polish dresiarz is the same look.

name: New rave
description: 2000s UK neon, psychedelic club fashion, popularised by labels such as Cassette Playa.

name: New Romantic
description: Flamboyant late-1970s London club scene of the Blitz Kids, with theatrical, androgynous dress.

name: Leather subculture
description: Post-war scene built on the ceremonial and erotic use of black leather attire and symbols.

name: Suedehead
description: Smarter later-1960s skinhead offshoot with Ben Sherman shirts and sharp dressing.

name: Ultras (football)
description: Football-ultra dress codified by brands: Adidas, Fred Perry, Stone Island, Burberry, Ellesse, Sergio Tacchini, C.P. Company.
